questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to go to Africa and since South Africa is the only country available in an exchange programme it was an easy choice.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Medium.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I did not really receive any from KU as I remember it.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: The SU international department were friendly but lacked competencies. First of all, none of the 400 hundred exchange students had been enrolled to the courses we had applied for before departure so we all had to start the semester 3 weeks after it had already begun as it was impossible to reach the international department by email and phone.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was easy enough as the housing was recommended by the university. However, I would recommend future students to find private housing elsewhere as you can better and bigger apartments with a pool area for the same amount of money or even less.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: They should check up on the neighbourhood they are searching in and see if they can find something which is secured with fences and guards for safety reasons.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Lots of paperwork back and forth for no good use as none were enrolled anyways as mentioned before.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: You had to just kick the door in at the SU international department if help wanted.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Medium

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Make sure you register for 40-50 ECTS. I only registered for 30 ECTS, but some of the classes rejected my enrollment so it would have been nice to have a safety net of other classes.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The academic level was high. The workload was significantly higher compared to KU.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Very different. Lots of closed books tests, assignments etc. You just have to memorize lots of theories etc. but don't really learn much about how to apply it in the real world.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Sport psychology
Sociology of work and employment
Scientific base of sport coaching

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: As an sport science student I would recommend Sport Psychology as the professor is really good. Scientific base of sport coaching is also really interesting. I love sociology and learning about different cultures and stuff so if people are in to learning more about the social structures post apartheid in South Africa I would recommend sociology of work and employment.

questions.answer: Data for the phone is really expensive, PCR-tests is about 300DKK as well,

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Obviously Covid-19 made everything more difficult, but there were lots of stuff to do.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Sport clubs, wine clubs, travel club

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I played at the tennis club which was nice. The travel club is also recommended.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Cape point, Waterfront at Cape Town, Addo Elephant (and the whole garden route), all the wine farms in and around of Stellenbosch

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Don't be shy. Reach out. People were really openminded.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Loadshedding (strømafbrydelse) which occured 4 hours a day in periods from 10-12 and 18-20. But the people and their lifestyle are extremely similar to our so I didn't struggle with that.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The openness and friendlyness.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Safety above all. Respect that you don't live in DK so you can't behave like you do at home and walk around alone in the night. 

Be curious and explore the city and country.

Expect a LOT of school work - more than you're used to.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: I stayed at the housing area called Academia where all the exchange students lived - it turned out. For that reason I would recommend the students to find private housing as the exchange students were from Germany and France mostly.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Meeting South African people

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The lack of safety and that you can't walk alone when it's dark and that there are so much crime and poverty.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: I would definitely recommend future students to rent or buy a car. It may cost a bit extra (not that expensive though), but it gives you great flexibility and gives you way more safety.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
